scope: Targeted primary-source review of implementable 3D geometry, perception, planning, safety-filter, and reachability methods for a fixed-base six-joint reBot first and a mobile manipulator later.
verification_scope: Paper metadata, abstracts and selected method/experiment sections, author or institutional repositories, and top-level license text were checked. Repositories and model binaries were not installed, executed, benchmarked, or audited for dependency licenses. This is a focused reading list, not an exhaustive systematic review.
implementation_status_in_this_workspace: These entries identify external reference implementations. None of these eight external packages was installed or reproduced as part of this research task. The existing local Poisson and OBB-pair velocity filters are separate preliminary implementations.

methods.title: Voxblox: Incremental 3D Euclidean Signed Distance Fields for On-Board MAV Planning
methods.venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
methods.publication_status: Published conference paper; official repository citation verified.
methods.code_kind: Author/institution reference mapping library; planning is a separate package.
methods.representation: Incremental voxel TSDF and Euclidean signed distance field (ESDF).
methods.input: Depth-derived point clouds with calibrated sensor poses.
methods.output: Surface mesh, ESDF distance queries and map data for downstream planners.
methods.validation: CPU mapping and onboard aerial-robot planning experiments; not articulated-arm validation.
limitations: The repository's ROS integration is ROS 1; ROS 2 Jazzy integration requires adaptation.
Map discretization, occlusion, unknown space and pose error remain relevant; an ESDF is not itself a controller or safety certificate.
methods.applicability: Useful CPU baseline for comparing map accuracy and latency before GPU mapping. Combine its environment field with B601 whole-link geometry, calibrated camera transforms, and a separate safety filter.
methods.jetson_evidence: CPU-oriented implementation; no benchmark was run on the user's Jetson.

methods.title: nvblox: GPU-Accelerated Incremental Signed Distance Field Mapping
methods.venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
methods.publication_status: Accepted ICRA 2024, verified on the author-submitted paper record.
methods.code_kind: Official NVIDIA core library with separate Isaac ROS integration.
methods.license: Apache-2.0 for the core nvblox repository; separately check integration and dependency licenses.
methods.representation: GPU voxel TSDF, ESDF, mesh and free-space information.
methods.input: Posed depth images and/or 3D LiDAR; optional color.
methods.output: Incremental 3D reconstruction and distance data queried by a planner or controller.
methods.validation: Paper includes mapping timings on Jetson Xavier AGX, desktop and laptop, plus robotic applications.
limitations: It provides a map, not an articulated safety policy; unknown space and stale/dynamic observations need explicit treatment.
Select a release compatible with the actual Jetson, JetPack, CUDA and ROS versions; latest documentation alone does not establish compatibility.
methods.applicability: Strong first RGB-D mapping candidate for the reBot pipeline, retaining conservative link geometry and an independent CBF controller.
methods.jetson_evidence: Official documentation targets Jetson devices; the paper's Xavier timings are not timings for this installation.

methods.title: Representing Robot Geometry as Distance Fields: Applications to Whole-body Manipulation
methods.venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA), pp. 15351-15357
methods.publication_status: Published conference paper; arXiv record and repository citation agree.
methods.code_kind: Author reference implementation, training utilities and pretrained Franka link models.
methods.license: MIT for RDF code; repository separately identifies the provided URDF as Apache-licensed.
methods.representation: Link-local signed distance approximations using Bernstein polynomials, composed through robot kinematics.
methods.input: Robot link meshes/kinematics, joint configurations and 3D query points.
methods.output: Robot-body SDF and gradients. The provided basis-function example uses analytic point gradients and numerical joint gradients.
methods.validation: Simulation and seven-axis Franka experiments, including dual-arm whole-body manipulation.
limitations: Learned approximation error must be measured; continuity is not a conservative distance-error bound.
Whole-body refers to articulated link geometry; this does not establish wheeled-base dynamics or perception safety.
methods.applicability: Train new link fields from B601 meshes and validate distance/gradient errors against conservative geometric collision queries. Useful alternative to current OBB proxies, not a ready B601 controller.
methods.jetson_evidence: README tested Python 3.8 and PyTorch 1.13; no user-Jetson timing or current-stack compatibility was verified.

methods.title: RAMP: Hierarchical Reactive Motion Planning for Manipulation Tasks Using Implicit Signed Distance Functions
methods.venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
methods.publication_status: Published conference paper; author-submitted record and author repository verified.
methods.code_kind: Author reference implementation; original Samsung project/repository links were unavailable when checked.
methods.license: CC-BY-NC-4.0; noncommercial restriction applies to the licensed material.
methods.representation: GPU robot-to-scene-point-cloud configuration SDF queries, shared by MPPI and a vector-field follower.
methods.input: URDF, joint limits/configuration, scene point cloud and goal.
methods.output: Predicted joint trajectories and reactive joint-velocity commands.
methods.validation: Simulated static/dynamic clutter and physical table-clearing experiments.
limitations: Predictive MPPI plus a reactive vector-field controller is not a CBF-QP implementation.
Provided simulation uses legacy Isaac Gym; README specifies Ubuntu 18.04/20.04 and Python 3.6-3.8 prerequisites.
methods.applicability: Useful predictive nominal-planner comparison. Reuse the documented planner/follower API with new B601 geometry rather than assuming its simulator works on Jetson Jazzy. Evaluate sensor coverage and tracking errors explicitly.
methods.jetson_evidence: No supported Jetson/aarch64 deployment or timing verified.

methods.title: Neural Configuration-Space Barriers for Manipulation Planning and Control
methods.venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering (T-ASE)
methods.publication_status: Accepted author manuscript explicitly identifies T-ASE 2026, DOI 10.1109/TASE.2026.3695092. Repository README still cites the 2025 preprint.
methods.code_kind: Author-lab reference code, training and pretrained xArm6 models, PyBullet planning/control examples.
methods.representation: Learned environment and self-collision configuration-distance fields, bubble planning and distributionally robust CBF-QP.
methods.input: Joint state, point cloud, learned robot models and sampled estimation uncertainty.
methods.output: Configuration-space path and filtered tracking control; CDF distances use joint-space units, not metres.
methods.validation: Six-DOF xArm6 simulation and depth-camera hardware experiments; controllers evaluated at 50 Hz.
limitations: Hardware moving-object velocities were estimated using ArUco markers; this is not general uninstrumented scene-flow estimation.
Neural uncertainty calibration and incomplete point-cloud coverage remain important; xArm6 weights do not transfer directly to B601.
methods.applicability: Closest research reference for the desired camera-to-high-DOF robust filter. Retrain B601 models and retain geometric validation. Test fixed-base first; mobile nonholonomy and torque feasibility require additional modeling.
methods.jetson_evidence: Training used an RTX 4090; no timing on this Jetson was verified.

methods.title: SAFER-Splat: A Control Barrier Function for Safe Navigation with Online Gaussian Splatting Maps
methods.venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
methods.publication_status: Accepted ICRA 2025, verified in author repository and paper record.
methods.code_kind: Author reference code; master contains simulation/filter code and the ros branch provides ROS 2 mapping/filter nodes.
methods.license: MIT for this repository; separate dependencies need their own review.
methods.representation: Online 3D Gaussian ellipsoids with geometry-aware CBF constraints and constraint pruning.
methods.input: RGB, time-of-flight point clouds, estimated camera poses, robot state and nominal acceleration.
methods.output: Gaussian reconstruction and filtered acceleration commands for an ellipsoidal robot.
methods.validation: Drone simulation and physical flights with onboard sensing but offboard RTX 4090 computation over Wi-Fi.
limitations: A drone ellipsoid is not a six-joint arm: link geometry, Jacobians and self-collision must be added.
Paper reports 1-4 mm barrier violations caused by low-level tracking; visual reconstruction is not ground-truth occupancy.
methods.applicability: Useful later perception-representation comparison, after ESDF and geometric baselines. Preserve conservative unknown-space handling and assess online training cost and map/control latency.
methods.jetson_evidence: Reported online performance is not Jetson-only evidence; dependency stack includes Nerfstudio and CUDA/PyTorch versions that need porting checks.

methods.title: Safe, Task-Consistent Manipulation with Operational Space Control Barrier Functions
methods.venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS), pp. 187-194
methods.publication_status: Published conference paper; official repository citation gives DOI 10.1109/IROS60139.2025.11246389.
methods.code_kind: Author-lab reference implementation with PyBullet examples; uses CBFpy/JAX.
methods.representation: Operational-space objectives with task-consistent CBF constraints and robot kinematics/dynamics.
methods.input: URDF, manually supplied collision model, joint state, task and barrier definitions.
methods.output: Filtered commands for velocity-controlled or torque-controlled manipulators.
methods.validation: Manipulator simulation and hardware; author code supports both input orders.
limitations: No complete RGB-D mapping front end; the provided Franka collision model is manually defined.
The README's planar PPR-chain mobile-base suggestion does not by itself enforce differential-drive nonholonomy.
methods.applicability: Strong next controller baseline for B601 after verifying URDF inertias and collision geometry. A future wheeled version needs an admissible-input mapping and acceleration/braking constraints.
methods.jetson_evidence: Author-tested Ubuntu 22.04 and Python 3.10/3.11; no user-Jetson benchmark or Python 3.12 validation was verified.

methods.title: RM4D: A Combined Reachability and Inverse Reachability Map for Common 6-/7-axis Robot Arms by Dimensionality Reduction to 4D
methods.venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
methods.publication_status: Presented at ICRA 2025 according to author repository; arXiv v1 retains its earlier submitted status.
methods.code_kind: Original author implementation, not the rai-opensource GPU fork.
methods.input: Robot kinematics/joint limits, sampled collision-free configurations and desired TCP pose.
methods.output: Reachability estimates and candidate base positions for a desired tool pose.
methods.validation: UR5e and Franka map studies plus mobile-manipulator grasp/base-placement example.
limitations: Reduction assumes 360-degree first-joint rotation and a 360-degree final wrist aligned with the tool approach vector; violations can introduce false positives.
A sampled reachable cell is not an environment-clear path, dynamic viability region, or payload/torque certificate.
methods.applicability: Useful reachability-map upgrade and future base-placement layer. Check B601 axis/TCP assumptions, build its own map, and verify candidates with IK and collision planning.
methods.jetson_evidence: Offline map construction can be separated from fast queries; no user-Jetson performance was measured.

supporting_reading.title: Safety-Critical Model Predictive Control with Discrete-Time Control Barrier Function
supporting_reading.role: Explicit predictive-CBF foundation: impose h(x[k+1]) >= (1-gamma) h(x[k]) along a modeled horizon, together with input constraints.
supporting_reading.code_status: Archived author reference implementation using MATLAB, YALMIP and IPOPT; examples are a 2D double integrator and racing, not a camera-guided manipulator.
supporting_reading.limitation: A B601 implementation needs articulated geometry, model and solver adaptation; sampled horizon constraints alone do not establish continuous inter-sample safety.

supporting_reading.year: 2022 online DOI; consult final IEEE issue metadata for issue year
supporting_reading.venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L), DOI 10.1109/LRA.2022.3227860
supporting_reading.license: No top-level license was visible in the checked author repository; reuse terms were not verified.

supporting_reading.title: Geometry-Aware Predictive Safety Filters on Humanoids: From Poisson Safety Functions to CBF Constrained MPC
supporting_reading.venue: IEEE-RAS International Conference on Humanoid Robots
supporting_reading.role: Direct theoretical extension from static Poisson fields to moving boundaries, geometry lifting and CBF-constrained predictive control.
supporting_reading.code_status: Paper/author material verified; no public author implementation was verified in this search. Do not list as a ready code baseline.

foundations_and_read_order.purpose: Understand world-space 3D TSDF versus ESDF, observed free space, calibration, voxel resolution and map latency.
Understand articulated robot-body geometry and why a 3D scene alone does not describe the six-dimensional configuration-space collision set.
Connect distance gradients to admissible joint commands; distinguish velocity and torque input models, learned approximation errors and uncertainty.
Distinguish one-step filtering, MPPI prediction and CBF-constrained MPC; inspect braking, feasibility, moving obstacles and inter-sample safety.
Add tool-pose reachability and inverse reachability for base placement without treating either as dynamic safe reachability.
Explore richer online scene representations after a measured ESDF and geometric baseline is working.

implementation_recommendation.first_fixed_base: Keep current geometric and Poisson baselines; add calibrated RGB-D observations and a compatible nvblox release. Query a full 3D ESDF around all modeled links, retain unknown-space and map-age checks, then compare a velocity CBF using the same nominal planner and geometry.
implementation_recommendation.research_comparison: Compare robot-centric RDF or NCSB after collecting B601-specific distance data and validating held-out worst-case distance/gradient error. Use RAMP for a predictive nominal-planner comparison; use OSCBF for task-consistent velocity/torque filtering. These roles are complementary, not interchangeable.
implementation_recommendation.mobile_extension: Use RM4D only to propose base placements. Model the actual wheeled-base input map, include base/torso/arm/gripper/payload geometry, maintain a common world frame and camera timestamps, and add stopping/acceleration/torque/stability constraints before interpreting a filter as whole-body protection.
unit_and_dimension_checks: An environment ESDF is a function of a 3D spatial point and normally returns metres; an articulated configuration has six joint variables, even though its workspace is drawn in 3D.
For a differentiable scene distance phi and link point p_i(q), b_i(q,t)=phi(p_i(q),t)-margin and db_i/dt=grad(phi)^T J_i(q) qdot + partial(phi)/partial(t). All relevant geometry rows are needed.
A learned configuration-space distance measures distance to contact in the chosen joint-coordinate metric; do not substitute its radian-valued threshold for a metre-valued ESDF margin.
Higher robot DOF is different from higher barrier relative degree. Torque/acceleration control requires the appropriate dynamic barrier derivative and a valid admissible-input set.
Kinematic reachability, collision-free planning and dynamic robust controlled invariance answer different questions; a reachability heatmap is not an HJ viability certificate.

verification_notes: Top-level license verification does not certify the licenses of bundled URDFs, datasets, pretrained weights or dependencies.
Author-reported rates and successes are tied to their hardware, geometry, sensors and test distributions; none establishes reBot/Jetson performance.
Public code availability was checked as of the verification date; no claim is made that every advertised experiment is immediately reproducible on the current ROS 2 Jazzy/aarch64 stack.
